headline: Highest risk is filesystem-based prompt injection and write-conflict: Mentat can read/write shared files and modify git state, while Taipy’s runnable/IO surfaces are undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat can read and write the filesystem and shares state via filesystem; Taipy’s IO surfaces are undocumented, so a shared-file bridge is plausible but not proven. If Taipy consumes files or generated artifacts as inputs, Mentat content could be treated as instructions. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Taipy reads files from the same workspace as Mentat outputs
IF Mentat writes attacker-controlled text into shared files
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
Review shared artifacts before Taipy consumes them
Use read-only mounts for Taipy inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code and has broad network egress to a configured model provider, while Taipy’s network egress is none. If both share a workspace, source code can flow into Mentat’s backend during normal operation. Taipy itself is not a leak path, but the pair still exposes code to a third party through Mentat.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same source tree
IF Mentat sends file contents to its configured model provider
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of Mentat’s working set
Use a local-only model backend for Mentat
Split workspaces by sensitivity
Audit which files Mentat uploads before use
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via filesystem. Taipy’s write or coordination capabilities are undocumented, so the safe assumption is that overlapping writes may occur if it also mutates the same workspace. Because git state corruption can be irreversible, uncertainty escalates to high.
conditions: IF Taipy writes to the same directory or git repo as Mentat
IF both agents run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Use separate git branches per agent
Add a file lock around shared paths
Review diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and Taipy is tagged for automation/job-scheduler use, so a plausible pipeline is Mentat output feeding Taipy-driven actions. Taipy’s verification behavior is undocumented, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced. The risk is medium because the output can be acted on without a human review step.
conditions: IF Taipy consumes Mentat-generated diffs or summaries as authoritative input
IF no human review gate exists before Taipy acts
mitigations: Require manual approval before downstream actions
Validate Mentat outputs against expected schemas
Log and diff all proposed changes
Limit Taipy to read-only analysis of Mentat output
requires-engineering: add verification checkpoints

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. Mentat handles model-provider API keys and source code; Taipy’s compliance posture is not described. With no concrete mismatch evidence, only a low residual compliance concern remains, and the other agent is not separately cited because no pairwise compliance pathway is established.
conditions: IF either agent is deployed under a policy requiring documented retention or residency controls
IF Taipy stores or exports the same source code under a different policy
mitigations: Confirm data residency for both deployments
Review retention settings for model-provider logs
Avoid sending regulated data to Mentat
Document which files Taipy stores or exports
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both tools
